text:
jordan: quick follow-up from today's all-hands: can we get a short checklist of what features land in the kernel refactor vs what stays at the runtime layer?

leah: specifically curious about which optimizations require model recompile vs just a runtime flag flip.

sam: high level: kernel refactor = execution primitives (attention, matmul kernels, quantized ops). Runtime layer = routing, batching, kv cache, orchestration. Most customers won't need to recompile models; the refactor exposes new backends that we can target transparently.

tony: add: some model-specific fused ops (e.g., rotary+caching fusion) will need a short compile step when you opt into q4/mixed paths. We plan a compatibility shim so old binaries still run.

jordan: timeline question: when will we have perf numbers for q4_xm vs q8 on the new kernels?

sam: expected microbenchmarks in 2 weeks, customer-facing benchmark docs in 4 weeks. We'll include p50/p95, memory, and token/s throughput across common sequence lengths.

leah: what about client-visible behavioral changes? e.g., tokenization differences or streaming latencies?

sam: no tokenizer change. Streaming should improve for long sequences because we flush earlier from the GPU. You might see slightly different chunking in responses (smaller early chunks) but model outputs are equivalent.

tony: mitigation for any canary regressions: automated rollback on metric breach, and a hotfix branch that disables new kernels but keeps runtime changes.

jordan: can you share the canary criteria?

sam: sure:

```
canary_criteria:
  percent_traffic: 3
  monitor: [p50_ms, p95_ms, errors_pct]
  thresholds:
    p50_ms: +15%
    p95_ms: +20%
    errors_pct: +0.4
  rollback: auto
```

leah: if we opt individual dedicated clusters into preview, will that affect billing or SLOs?

sam: billing unchanged. Preview clusters are isolated TGs; we won't change SLOs for committed Dedicated clusters unless customer opts into the preview SLA. We'll add a clear consent flow in Console.

runtime-bot: Scheduled deploy: runtime/refactor/canary/2026-11-12T09:00Z -> canary zone. Owners: @tony, @sam. CI status: passing.

tony: I'll post heap and KV-trim knobs after the deploy so folks can toggle during the test window.

jordan: awesome, thanks. I'll consolidate these answers into the all-hands notes and flag any follow-ups.
